dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin.
Hi, yeah, Kevin. Um, this is Daniel Rahman. I know it's, what, almost seven at night, so I'm guessing City Hall's closed and this is the after-hours line, right?
Yep, City Hall's closed for the day, but this line's open for storm and drainage stuff. What's going on?
Okay, good. So I manage a property at 292 Eustis Avenue, up Historic Hill, and there's a catch basin at the corner that's totally clogged. Hold on, sorry, I'm typing this into my notes, one sec.
No problem, take your time.

Sorry, I know the keyboard comes through like I'm shouting. Anyway, the basin is packed with leaves, and every time it rains the water just backs up and comes right into the driveway. It's been like that since the coastal storm, the one Friday into Saturday, three days ago.
Okay, so catch basin at the corner of Eustis, clogged with leaves, water backing into the driveway at 292. Did I get that right?

Yeah, that's it. And this isn't new, I've been dealing with this, the leaves just sit there every fall and nobody comes to clear them. So I went out today, I got down on my knees and pulled the leaves off the grate by hand. Wet, disgusting. And it worked, for like ten minutes. Then more stuff washed down and it's clogged again.
Yeah, that'll happen. If the pipe under it is packed, clearing the grate only does so much. Is there standing water there right now?

Right now it's a big puddle, [pause] sorry, hang on, I'm closing a door. It's a big puddle across the bottom of the driveway, not in the building, but the tenants can't get their cars in without driving through it. And it's January, so at night it's going to be ice.
Right, that's a problem. Alright, I'm writing this up. Corner catch basin, Eustis Avenue, blocked with leaf debris, ponding into the driveway at 292. Any cross street you want me to put down?
It's the corner just down from the driveway, toward the harbor side. I don't remember the cross street offhand. Honestly, the crew would see it. It's the only basin on that corner.
That's fine, the address will get them close. And you're the property manager, not the owner?

Right, property manager. I answer for it anyway, so when tenants are calling me at dinner about their cars, it's on me. Which is why I'm asking. Is a work order going to be opened for this? And can you tell me a date? Not 'sometime', an actual date.

I'm opening the work order now, so yes, it'll be in the system tonight. As for a date, I can't see the crew schedule from this screen. After a storm like that they've got a backlog of basins all over the city, so I can't promise you a day.
Okay, but that's what I got last time too, backlog. That's the answer every time. I need something I can tell the tenants. Tomorrow, this week, next week?

Fair. I'll mark it as ponding into a private driveway with freezing risk, which does bump the priority a bit. The supervisor looks at the new orders first thing in the morning, and I'll note that you want a scheduled date. Someone from the office should be able to call you back with it.
Alright. So the callback, that'd be tomorrow?
The office opens in the morning, so tomorrow is the earliest they'd see it. I can't swear they'll get to the call tomorrow, but it'll be at the top of the pile. What number do you want on it?
401-555-0163, got it. And that's Daniel Rahman, R-A-H-M-A-N?
Yep, that's right. Sorry, one more second, I'm typing the order thing down so I remember what you said.
Go ahead. The order is for the catch basin at the corner by 292 Eustis Avenue, debris clearing, callback requested with a scheduled date.
Perfect. And in the meantime, is there anything I'm allowed to do? Because I'll go out again with a rake if it helps, I just don't want to do something dumb and get in trouble.

Clearing leaves off the top of the grate is fine, that's actually helpful. Just don't pull the grate up or reach down into the basin, and stay out of the street if cars are coming, especially in the dark.
Okay. No, I wasn't going to pull the grate. It's heavy anyway. I'll just keep the top clear and put some salt down by the driveway tonight.
That works. If it gets bad overnight, like the water's reaching a building or the street's flooding, call this line back and we'll get somebody on it.
Alright. I'd just like to not have to call a fourth time about the same corner. Please make sure the note says that.
I'll put it in the notes that this has been reported before and you're looking for a firm date. That's the best I can do from here.
Okay. Thanks, Kevin. I appreciate you writing it down at least.
Sure thing. Stay warm out there, Daniel. Somebody will be in touch.
Yeah. Thanks. Bye.
